Generalized likelihood-ratio test for VCMoE coefficient variation

Source: R/glrt.R
vcmoe_glrt.Rd

Generalized likelihood-ratio test for VCMoE coefficient variation

Usage

vcmoe_glrt(
  fit,
  data,
  test = c("coefficient", "constant_block", "constant_all"),
  coefficient_set = c("expert", "gating", "sigma", "theta"),
  component = NULL,
  term = NULL,
  calibration = c("none", "bootstrap", "analytic_epanechnikov", "both",
    "parametric_bootstrap"),
  B = 200L,
  seed = NULL,
  control = list(),
  refit_control = list(),
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

fit

A vcmoe fit.

data

Original data frame used to fit fit.

test

Test type. "coefficient" tests one coefficient function; "constant_block" tests all expert or gating functions jointly; "constant_all" tests all fitted coefficient functions jointly.

coefficient_set

Coefficient block for coefficient-specific or block-constant tests.

component

Component label or index for coefficient-specific tests.

term

Term name for coefficient-specific tests.

calibration

Calibration method. The default "none" returns the statistic without attaching a reference distribution. "analytic_epanechnikov" uses the Epanechnikov modified chi-square approximation; "bootstrap" uses parametric bootstrap calibration; "both" reports both.

B

Number of bootstrap calibration replicates.

seed

Optional random seed.

control

Controls for constrained null optimization and diagnostics: lambda_type ("observation", the default; "fit_objective", the scale used by VCMoE 0.2.0; or "grid_sum"), strict (default FALSE), C_const (default 1), null_projection for joint-path nulls ("uniform", the default, or "sample_weighted", the rule of VCMoE 0.2.0), maxit and reltol for the null optimizer, and lambda_tol.

refit_control

Controls overriding bootstrap full-model refits.

verbose

Whether to message bootstrap progress.

Value

A vcmoe_glrt object.

Details

Statistic. lambda is the difference between the full and null observation-level mixture log-likelihoods, sum_i log sum_k pi_k(u_i) f_k(y_i; u_i), with each coefficient path evaluated at the observation's own u_i by the linear interpolation used by predict.vcmoe(). This is the likelihood of the Wilks-type result for local likelihood ratio tests. lambda_type = "fit_objective" instead uses the objective the engine maximises (the sum of grid-point local likelihoods for local-grid fits, the nearest-grid observation likelihood for joint-path fits). A sum over grid points counts each observation about 1 / (grid spacing) times, so analytic p-values on that scale are far too small; it is kept only to reproduce earlier results. The fitted-objective ratio is always reported as lambda_fit_objective, and a negative value blocks the test as a null-optimizer failure. A negative observation-level ratio is a valid, non-significant outcome.

Analytic calibration. The statistic rK * max(lambda, 0) is compared with a chi-square distribution with delta = rK * p_test * C_const * |U| * (K(0) - int K^2 / 2) / h degrees of freedom, where p_test is the number of coefficient functions constrained under the null: 1 for one coefficient function, k - 1 contrasts for a gating term, and the whole block for block tests. The approximation is intended for independent observations and joint-path fits; for local-grid fits it has not been validated and settings$theory_status says so. With clustered observations (for example cells from the same donor), use the cluster-robust path tests of vcmoe_confband() instead.

Null fits. Local-grid fits use a constrained BFGS null optimizer. Joint-path fits use a grid-projected null: after every M-step each constrained coefficient path is replaced by its average over the grid points (equal weights by default; with null_projection = "sample_weighted", weights proportional to the number of observations assigned to each nearest grid point), and constrained local slopes are set to zero. An optimizer error, or a null fit that beats the full fit on the fitted objective, blocks the test and returns an NA p-value. A null fit that stops at its iteration limit gives a p-value with the warning null_optimizer_not_fully_converged and null_converged = FALSE; strict = TRUE blocks it, together with every other warning.

Bootstrap. Bootstrap refits preserve the engine of fit. Each refit numbers its components independently, so a component-specific test follows the matched reference component into the refit; for a gating contrast with k >= 3 both components of the contrast are followed. Draws whose null optimizer failed, or whose null beats the full refit, are excluded; draws whose null fit only reached its iteration limit are kept. bootstrap_counts reports the requested, successful and excluded draws.
